# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 15
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 15

---

*[The transfiguration vision. Moses and Elijah appear. Peter's response.]*

1. And I, Peter, answered and said to him: "Lord, I want to see also those men and women who had not sinned, so that I may know them."

2. And the Lord answered and said to me: "Be it so. And let us go to the mountain and pray."

3. And we went and prayed, and there appeared to us two men standing before the Lord toward the east.

4. And I could not look upon their faces because of the light that was from their faces. For their faces were shining as the light of the sun, and their clothing was shining, and I cannot describe it. And they were clothed in white linen.

5. When I saw them I was greatly afraid. And the Lord said to me: "These are your brothers the righteous. These are your fathers and these are they who received the eternal life."

6. And I said to him: "How is it possible that these should be with you, when the world has not yet passed away? And where has the flesh gone from them?"

7. And the Lord answered me: "I will show you also what I have shown to you before this. Go and bring it that I may see."

8. And then suddenly two men came from the east again, who shone with great light, and they were more luminous than the sun, and their raiment was wonderful.

9. I could not look at them because of the light that was in them. And there came a voice from them, as the voice of the lightning of thunder.

10. And I asked one of them: "Who are you?"

11. And he said: "I am Moses, the lawgiver, and he who is with me is Elijah the prophet."

12. And they entered into the cloud, and I and the others saw the shape of the Lord and the brightness of his glory.

---
*EMET note: This chapter overlaps with and interprets the Transfiguration (Matt 17; Mark 9; Luke 9). The APE makes explicit what the canonical accounts leave unclear — the two figures are Moses and Elijah, and the scene is eschatological, not merely anticipatory.*
